text: Oh, how fascinating it was and how she loved sitting here. <break time="0.8s" /> And watching it all. <break time="0.8s" /> For it was like a play. <break time="0.8s" /> Exactly like a play. <break time="0.8s" /> Who could believe. <break time="0.8s" /> That the sky at the back. <break time="0.8s" /> So blue and so still above the trees. <break time="0.8s" /> Was not simply painted on a great canvas. <break time="0.8s" /> It was not until a little brown dog. <break time="0.8s" /> Trotted on solemnly. <break time="0.8s" /> And then slowly trotted off. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a little theater dog. <break time="0.8s" /> That Miss Brill discovered. <break time="0.8s" /> What made it so exciting. <break time="0.8s" /> They were all on the stage. <break time="0.8s" /> And they were not merely the audience, looking on but actors. <break time="0.8s" /> And even she had a part. <break time="0.8s" /> And came every Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> No doubt somebody would have noticed. <break time="0.8s" /> If she had not been there. <break time="0.8s" /> And that was why. <break time="0.8s" /> She always left home at the same time. <break time="0.8s" /> So as not to be late. <break time="0.8s" /> It also explained. <break time="0.8s" /> Why she had a queer, shy feeling. <break time="0.8s" /> When she told her English pupils. <break time="0.8s" /> How she spent her Sunday afternoons. <break time="0.8s" /> She thought of the old invalid gentleman. <break time="0.8s" /> To whom she read the newspaper. <break time="0.8s" /> Four afternoons a week. <break time="0.8s" /> And she imagined telling him. <break time="0.8s" /> I have been an actress for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> As the band played on she looked smiling at everyone. <break time="0.8s" /> With tears in her eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking, Yes, we understand. <break time="0.8s" /> Though what they understood. <break time="0.8s" /> She did not know.
